ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening must be performed before engagement and refreshed at least every 90 calendar days for all UBOs, directors, officers, authorized signatories, and high-risk counterparties. Screening systems must cover consolidated OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists, UN Security Council sanctions resolutions, EU consolidated financial sanctions, the Korean FIU designated list, and sanctions administered by the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Ministry of Economy and Finance. PEP status including family members and close associates must be verified using licensed commercial databases; positive hits trigger enhanced due diligence, written source-of-funds evidence, and senior management approval. This protocol applies notwithstanding the Low_Risk_Standard banking AML rating for the PropTech platform.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (IROS) at https://www.iros.go.kr
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered legal name must be in Hangul under the Commercial Act; English names may appear only in the Articles of Association or as a transliterated trade name. Transliteration from Korean to English follows the Revised Romanization of Korean. Four-tier naming convention is required: (1) distinctive name identifier, (2) business scope qualifier, (3) entity type designator Yuhan Hoesa, and (4) optional matching English name. Chinese characters are not used as the primary registered legal name in Korea.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 14 days of receiving a name rejection notice, the applicant may submit a written reconsideration request to the Chief Judge of the competent District Court Registration Office, accompanied by the original IROS search result screenshots and a legal memorandum distinguishing the proposed name from cited prior registrations. If reconsideration is denied, file a formal objection under the Act on Registration of Non-Contentious Proceedings before the same district court; a judicial decision is typically rendered within 30 days. To avoid delay, the applicant may simultaneously file a fresh name reservation application with an alternative transliteration. Reserved names may be renewed before expiry by paying the statutory reservation fee again.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual office with only a mail-forwarding address is not recommended and may be rejected by both the National Tax Service and Korean banks. Korean commercial registration can accept a managed serviced office address if the provider supplies an official address registration confirmation and the space is available for service of process. For a PropTech SaaS platform using Stripe and ACH, a dedicated co-working suite with a visible reception sign, meeting room facility, lease agreement, and dedicated telephone/contact line is the minimum prudent structure. Without local substance such as lease, personnel, or accounting records, Korean banks may decline current account opening and tax authorities may disregard the registered office.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: approximately 15% unannounced physical inspection within the first 12 months where a virtual office is used, rising to 35% if the tax filing address is shared by multiple shell entities or payroll/employment records are absent. Inspection trigger checklist: (1) exterior sign or building directory listing; (2) on-site employee or authorized representative available during business hours; (3) original lease or service contract; (4) utility bills in the company name; (5) accounting records physically retrievable at the address; (6) no indication of letterbox-only operations; and (7) consistency of registered address with the customer-facing privacy policy.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, Chapter II, Section 3 (Limited Liability Company), Articles 543 through 613, as amended; Commercial Registration Act, as amended; Foreign Investment Promotion Act and its Enforcement Decree where a non-resident member subscribes capital contributions.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registration Division of the District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office; online filing through iROS, the Internet Registry Office operated by the Supreme Court of Korea.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Articles of Incorporation and Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Limited Liability Company (Yuhan Hoesa); the final conclusive certificate is the Certificate of Registered Matters issued by the District Court registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None: Korean law does not impose a minimum paid-up capital for a Yuhan Hoesa. Nevertheless, the total declared capital in the Articles of Incorporation must be fully paid in or fully covered by non-cash contributions before registration. For cash contributions, the funds must be deposited into a Korean bank account and evidenced by a certificate of capital payment issued by the bank. Korean law does not require a separate blocked escrow account or court-supervised escrow deposit for Yuhan Hoesa formation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FORMAL PRO-FORMA UNANIMOUS WRITTEN CONSENT OF FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [INSERT KOREAN YUHAN HOESA NAME], A LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY REGISTERED UNDER THE LAWS OF THE REPUBLIC OF KOREA. WHEREAS, the company is a Yuhan Hoesa (limited liability company) formed under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea; WHEREAS, the initial members have subscribed to the aggregate contributed capital of the company in the amount of [KRW CURRENCY AMOUNT], currently held in a corporate capital deposit account at a commercial bank; WHEREAS, the Articles of Incorporation require the first board of directors to adopt the organizational structure and to authorize operational matters before the company transacts any business; WHEREAS, the following persons have been designated in the Articles as directors of the company: [DIRECTOR 1], [DIRECTOR 2], and [DIRECTOR 3, IF APPLICABLE], and the undersigned directors constitute a quorum and have unanimously waived notice of a statutory meeting. NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED AS FOLLOWS: 1. CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION AND CONTRIBUTION. The subscription by the founding members to the entire declared capital in the amount of [KRW CURRENCY AMOUNT] is ratified and confirmed. The board confirms that all in-kind contributions, if any, have been appraised and the statutory statement of contribution has been prepared. The Representative Director is directed to deposit or cause to be deposited all outstanding cash contributions without delay and to furnish the court registry with the capital payment certificate upon registration. 2. REGISTERED OFFICE. The registered office of the company at [COMPLETE STREET ADDRESS, REPUBLIC OF KOREA] is hereby adopted. The Representative Director is authorized to execute the office lease and to file the registered office with the competent District Court Registry. Any change of registered office shall require a board resolution and an amendment registration. 3. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS. [DIRECTOR 1] is appointed Representative Director and Chief Executive Officer of the company, and shall serve as the legal representative of the company. [DIRECTOR 2] is appointed Director and Chief Operating Officer; [DIRECTOR 3, IF APPLICABLE] is appointed Auditor if required by law or if the Articles so provide. All officers are authorized, within the scope of the law, to sign and file every necessary document with government registries. 4. BANKING AUTHORIZATION. The primary banking relationship shall be established at [BANK], [BRANCH]. The Representative Director, together with [FINANCE OFFICER], shall open all corporate accounts. The Representative Director is authorized to execute bank mandates, signature cards, online banking agreements and settlement instructions. Two signatures, being the Representative Director and one other director, shall be required for any withdrawal, guarantee or other banking commitment in excess of [KRW AMOUNT], unless otherwise authorized by a specific board resolution. 5. CORPORATE SEAL AND DOCUMENTS. The corporate seal of the company adopted by the board is approved. The Representative Director shall register the seal at the relevant registry, if required, and shall preserve custody of the common seal. 6. GOVERNANCE AND BOOKS. The first accounting period shall commence on [START DATE] and end on [END DATE]. Management shall maintain books and records in accordance with Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles and the Commercial Act, and the Auditor shall perform the statutory audit, if any. 7. GENERAL DELEGATION. Each statutory officer is authorized to take all additional actions, execute all agreements, file all notices and do all other acts as may be required to implement this resolution under Korean law. This consent may be executed in counterparts and is effective as of the date written below.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of Articles of Incorporation and due diligence on founding persons
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public licensed by the Korean Ministry of Justice and registered with the Korean Notary Association.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Articles of Incorporation containing all statutory particulars, including the corporate name ending in Yuhan Hoesa, the business purpose covering software development and PropTech SaaS services, the registered office address, the amount of contributed capital, the name of each member, the contribution value and method, and the names of directors and auditor if any. All founding members must personally execute the Articles in the presence of a Korean notary public, or by a notarized power of attorney for absent foreign members. The notary verifies identity, official passport and legal capacity. Foreign corporate members must supply an apostilled certificate of incorporation and proof of authority; all non-Korean documents require official English or Korean translations.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Incorporation for Yuhan Hoesa
Passport copies of all founding members
Notarized power of attorney for representatives executing for absent members
Apostilled proof of legal existence of foreign corporate member, if any
Certificate of personal seal or equivalent signature confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary refuses authentication due to missing legalization, correct the Articles by unanimous consent and re-submit; provide any missing apostille, translation or identity evidence within one business day.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital contribution deposit and bank certificate of payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Korean commercial bank or authorized foreign exchange bank.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a capital deposit account with a licensed Korean bank in the name of the company or the promoter. Each member must transfer the subscribed capital amount or deposit cash, and receive a certificate of capital deposit from the bank. If a member is a foreign investor, the remittance must go through an authorized foreign exchange bank and, before payment, a foreign investment report must be filed under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act to preserve qualified foreign investment status and tax benefits. The Representative Director should instruct the bank to hold the funds until incorporation; after court registration the account is converted into the company's ordinary operating account. Obtain the final balance certificate and payment confirmation for attachment to the registration application.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Identity documents of all members
Capital subscription statement
Funds remittance records or cash deposit slips
Bank certificate of capital payment
Foreign investment report acknowledgement, if non-resident member is involved
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank questions beneficial ownership or source of funds, provide a corporate ownership declaration and source-of-funds evidence; if a wire is delayed, issue new remittance instructions; if the foreign exchange report is incomplete, amend it through the reporting bank before payment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registration Division of the District Court with jurisdiction over the registered office, using iROS online filing or in-person submission.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After notarization and capital payment, file the incorporation registration with the local District Court registry. The application must include the court-prescribed registration form, the notarized Articles, written consents of directors and auditor, the capital payment certificate, identity records of members, registered office lease or owner consent, and a power of attorney if filed by an agent. Pay the registration tax and education surtax. The court examines compliance with the Commercial Act and, once satisfied, enters the company into the commercial register and issues the Certificate of Registered Matters confirming corporate existence. The effective date of incorporation is the date of court registration.
required_dossiers: Completed commercial registration application form
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Certificate of capital payment or capital deposit
Consent forms of directors and auditor, if any
Registered office lease agreement or owner's written consent
Power of attorney if application is filed by a professional agent
Receipt of registration tax payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a correction notice, submit all supplementary evidence within the statutory correction period; if registration is rejected, file a corrected application or an administrative appeal with the registry chief, and re-submit once the defect is cured.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business registration for tax and invoicing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service through Hometax or the local district tax office having jurisdiction over the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After court registration, the company must register its business with the National Tax Service before conducting revenue-generating activities. This business registration certificate establishes the corporate number used for VAT, corporate income tax, withholding tax and electronic tax invoices. File the application using the Certificate of Registered Matters, the Articles, the lease contract, identity documents and the bank certificate. Select the Korean Standard Industrial Classification corresponding to ISIC 6201 for software and online service activities. The tax office issues a business registration certificate with the corporate registration number. The company must then update its bank and vendor records and comply with Korean tax invoice and bookkeeping obligations.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Registered Matters
Business registration application form
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Registered office lease contract
Corporate seal or seal registration certificate
Bank certificate and capital payment confirmation
Director identification and power of attorney, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office queries the application, submit the missing lease, identity or classification data; if the wrong business classification is entered, file a correction before issuing invoices to avoid tax notice mismatches.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate seal registration, bank account activation and social insurance compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local District Court Registry, the corporate bank branch, National Pension Service, National Health Insurance Service, Korea Employment Information Service, Korea Workers' Compensation and Welfare Service, and the Ministry of Employment and Labor as applicable.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Immediately after business registration, complete the administrative governance steps: register the corporate seal with the court registry if a seal registration card will be used; activate the corporate bank account with the approved signatory list; register all directors and employees with the four social insurance schemes, namely national pension, national health insurance, employment insurance and industrial accident compensation insurance; post employment rules with the Ministry of Employment and Labor if the company has ten or more employees; and, for cloud SaaS activities, confirm that no separate telecommunications platform license is required under the provided scope. Any foreign shareholding must also be reported under foreign investment reporting and foreign exchange rules.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Registered Matters
Corporate seal registration card, if obtained
Authorized bank signatory forms
Employee list and identity documents
Employment contracts
Social insurance registration forms
Foreign investment report certificate, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If social insurance registration is missed, file late registrations and pay any arrear contributions; late penalties can be mitigated by voluntary disclosure; if the bank requires additional beneficial ownership evidence, provide the corporate registry extract and ownership chart.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable; ISIC 6201 involves a pure digital cloud-based PropTech SaaS platform with no manufacturing, chemical processing, assembly, or warehousing facility. If only a conventional commercial office is leased, the local municipal building office and the local fire department are the only authorities relevant to ordinary commercial occupancy.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable; no industrial operating license, factory establishment permit, or manufacturing license is required for the digital SaaS operations described in the target payload.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable; the Ministry of Environment would be the competent authority only for physical development projects requiring an Environmental Impact Assessment, and no physical project is present here.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt/Not Applicable; no full Environmental Impact Assessment, preliminary EIA consultation, or environmental registration is triggered by software development or cloud-based property technology services.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable; the operation generates no wastewater discharge, VOC emissions, combustion emissions, hazardous waste storage, or chemical handling that would invoke quantitative environmental thresholds under the Korean Clean Air Conservation Act, Water Environment Conservation Act, or Wastes Control Act.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable for industrial or civil-defense fire permits; a standard commercial office must nevertheless satisfy basic fire safety requirements under the Korean Fire Service Act, including maintenance of fire extinguishers, unobstructed exits and an evacuation plan, and must comply with the Occupational Safety and Health Act for office-based software employees. No structural load certificate, civil-defense clearance, or special factory fire-safety certification is required.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea, operating the HomeTax electronic tax portal at hometax.go.kr, together with the Korea Customs Service for customs clearance through UNI-PASS at unipass.customs.go.kr
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign non-resident entity engaged in Korean-source taxable supply must obtain a Korean Business Registration Number (BRN) by filing an application with the local district tax office of the National Tax Service (NTS) via HomeTax. The procedure requires (1) completing the business registration application form; (2) submitting the foreign certificate of incorporation or equivalent registry extract; (3) providing the statutory representative or tax representative's power of attorney and identity documentation; (4) declaring the actual place of business in Korea or confirming the absence of a fixed place and appointing a tax representative for VAT compliance; (5) submitting the lease contract or free-use letter for the Korean office where a fixed place exists; and (6) obtaining the 10-digit BRN certificate, which is simultaneously the Korean VAT identification number. For foreign online or digital service providers without a domestic fixed place of business, the NTS requires VAT registration through the foreign non-resident business track of HomeTax, with the same BRN issuance, and the foreign entity must aggregate all Korean web sales and report VAT under the Value-Added Tax Act. Electronic filing is mandatory through HomeTax or an approved electronic tax invoice integration service.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The Republic of Korea has no check-the-box pass-through election for limited companies; a Yuhan Hoesa is always taxed as a separate entity under the Corporate Tax Act. No hybrid mismatch election is available at the entity classification stage.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general turnover threshold for VAT registration; every business supplying taxable goods or services in Korea must register for VAT regardless of annual turnover. Reduced compliance for simplified taxpayer status applies for an individually owned small business with annual taxable turnover not exceeding KRW 80,000,000, but the simplified taxpayer is still registered and must issue cash receipts; a foreign incorporated PropTech company will not qualify for simplified taxpayer status when operating as a Yuhan Hoesa and must maintain full VAT registration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Korea operates a mandatory electronic tax invoice (e-invoice) system under Articles 32 and 32-2 of the Value-Added Tax Act. Registered VAT businesses must issue e-invoices through HomeTax, an approved electronic tax invoice service provider, or direct EDI linkage, and transmit the invoice data to the NTS under the statutory electronic reporting timeline. All tax invoices for supplies subject to VAT must include the BRN, the recipient's BRN, supply value, VAT amount, and supply date. The system includes near-real-time digital validation and anti-abuse checks; retail supplies to final consumers are supported by a mandatory cash receipt and credit card receipt system that feeds transaction data to the NTS, substantially reducing VAT leakage. No physical digital stamp is required for ordinary B2B SaaS invoices, but e-invoice records must remain auditable and transmitted through the NTS-approved protocol.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under the Value-Added Tax Act of the Republic of Korea, a zero rate of VAT applies to (1) export of goods where the goods are removed from Korea under an export declaration accepted by the Korea Customs Service; (2) services rendered to a foreign client in connection with exported tangible goods; and (3) digital services or electronically supplied services provided by a Korean VAT-registered business to a non-resident overseas recipient for use wholly outside Korea, provided the contract, place-of-supply rules, and business reality demonstrate that the benefit is consumed outside Korea. For PropTech SaaS subscriptions sold to foreign real estate landlords or overseas platform users, zero-rating is available only when the supply is not regarded as a domestic supply under the statutory place-of-supply rules and the exporter retains full documentation proving both export and foreign-exchange recovery.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (export bill of entry / export declaration certificate) accepted by the Korea Customs Service under the Customs Act
Bill of Lading for marine freight or Air Waybill for air freight showing the Korean shipper and foreign ultimate consignee
Commercial invoice and packing list describing the exported digital service or the physical media/goods

Inward Remittance Certificate (foreign exchange purchase or collection certificate) issued by a Korean foreign exchange bank or receipt certificate under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act demonstrating repatriation of export proceeds
Service contract or order agreement identifying the non-resident recipient and confirming the offshore place of supply for digitally supplied SaaS services
Bank statement or SWIFT/telegraphic transfer advisory matching the invoice value and remittance period
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The National Tax Service and Korea Customs Service conduct document-based and post-clearance audits to verify export zero-rating claims. If an exporter fails to prove physical export, foreign exchange collection within the statutory 180-day period, or the offshore consumption of digital services, the zero-rated amount is recharacterized as taxable domestic supply and assessed VAT of 10% plus interest and additional tax. Penalties include negligence penalties for false or unsubstantiated tax invoices ranging up to 40% of the supply value, separate aggravated penalties for issuance of fictitious electronic tax invoices, and criminal referral for tax evasion where fraudulent documentation is identified. Foreign exchange non-repatriation is also subject to penalty under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, including the revocation of export acceptance and clawback of tax privileges.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) acting jointly with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) as the foreign exchange administrative authority under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and its Enforcement Decree, with certified foreign exchange banks delegated execution and reporting powers via the Korea Foreign Exchange Information System (KFEIS)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a lightly managed KRW float with full convertibility for current account transactions and ordinary operational service payments, while the capital account remains regulated and transaction-specific. The Foreign Exchange Transactions Act permits almost all current account disbursements such as software royalties, SaaS subscription fees, and dividend remittances to be executed upon presentation to a foreign exchange bank of invoice, contract, tax certificate, and board resolution evidence. Capital account inflows such as foreign direct investment (FDI), share subscriptions, trustman type capital contributions or financial borrowings must be declared to KFEIS or, for direct investment exceeding regulatory thresholds, reported under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act (FIPA). There is no absolute Ban against profit repatriation: non-resident shareholders may remit dividends once audited retained earnings are confirmed, withholding tax is paid, and the bank receives a dividend distribution resolution plus tax records. However, if accumulated impairment losses exist, dividend payments are prohibited. Export proceeds including SaaS/PropTech subscription receipts must be repatriated to South Korea and either deposited into a domestic foreign currency account or sold for KRW; the Central Bank does not ration dollars, but all settlement receipts must carry permissible transactional purpose codes and be screened against the bank's AML surveillance. Capital inflow to the Korean LLC is treated as FDI and, upon registration and report completion, subsequent repatriation of the invested capital is generally unrestricted. The regime is therefore commercially accessible but documentary compliance and purpose-code integrity are strictly enforced, and Korean banks will not service flows that circumvent or evade these reporting duties.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, exporters of SaaS and software services are required to receive export proceeds through a certified foreign exchange bank within 18 months of the invoice date. The statutory surrender duty is satisfied by repatriating 100% of proceeds into a domestic foreign-currency operating account or by selling 100% to the bank for KRW; there is no fractional conversion ratio. If the bank permits an overseas receipt account, that structure must be pre-declared and reported to KFEIS.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account for Foreign Direct Investment; Basic Operational KRW Currency Account
Basic Operational KRW Currency Account and Foreign Currency Collection Account
Capital Escrow Account for Share Capital Injection; Basic Operational KRW Account
Foreign Currency Operating Account and KRW Settlement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. An offshore digital EMI such as Wise, Revolut Business, or Rapyd is not permitted to open a KRW deposit account or act as the primary legal clearing rail for a Korean resident corporate entity. The Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and Electronic Financial Transactions Act require cross-border KRW intermediation to be executed by a licensed foreign exchange bank; EMIs may only provide front-end invoicing, card acquirer processing, or non-KRW collection where the ultimate settlement is routed through a Korean bank. The treasury design should therefore install domestic Tier-1 banks as the owner of the KRW liquidity rails and treat any EMI as a supplementary non-KRW invoicing interface, never as the account house for the Korean LLC tax treasury.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Yes, physical presence is mandated for initial onboarding. Korean financial institutions are subject to the Real Name Financial Transactions Act and the Act on Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Transaction Information, which require at least one statutory director or a responsible officer holding a notarized and apostilled Power of Attorney to appear in branch. The bank must verify the director's resident registration identity and collect original company documents. Remote video KYC may accelerate the preliminary questionnaire, but in-branch verification or an official consular-issued verification record is necessary. For a non-resident founder without a Korean resident director, the bank's compliance committee may require the founder to visit Korea, or accept a specialised Korean legal firm as an authorized proxy holder with additional three-way verification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Distributed beneficial ownership through non-resident venture funds and intermediate SPV layers that complicate the ultimate beneficial owner declaration under FATF recommendation 24.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A certified copy of the Korean LLC charter, a full shareholder register and chain, signed UBO declaration for each natural person holding or controlling more than 25% of the entity, audited financial statements of each SPV, passport copies and tax numbers of ultimate principals, the KFEIS foreign investor report, the Foreign Investment Promotion Act filing receipt, and a notarized board resolution designating the Korean bank as depositary.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PropTech revenue touching real-estate projects which may involve quasi-trust flows, high-risk property settlement amounts, or screening against the Special Law on Proceeds from Serious Crimes.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed SaaS master subscription agreements, customer onboarding records with business registration and sanctions screening outputs, a monthly transaction ledger showing tenant screening and rent-monitoring fees, third-party SOC 2 and AML audit reports, board-approved fee tariff, landlord verification files when distributions are made, and commercial real estate deal evidence for any large incidental inflows.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The Korean resident director may be a foreign national or a local nominee representative rather than the true operational founder, exposing the account to shell-risk classification.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Tax clearance certificate and resident registration card of the director, employment contract evidencing substantive management duties, proof of domestic physical operations including office lease and utility bills in the entity name, payroll filings with the National Pension Service and health insurer, board minutes appointing the director as the bank relationship officer, and a written confirmation that no nominee agreement exists.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial paid-in capital injection exceeding KRW 500 million without sufficient trail of lawful source of funds from offshore entrepreneurial wealth or venture capital proceeds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified credit-screening file sourced from the remitting institution, twelve-month personal or venture-fund bank statements, executed investment agreement and valuation cap table, prior tax returns of the founders or fund, corporate registration of the investor, signed source-of-wealth declaration, and documentary evidence that the funds are not commingled with real-estate escrow or cryptocurrency proceeds.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injection must be structured as a lawful foreign direct investment (FDI) wire. Funds should arrive via SWIFT MT103 from the non-resident shareholder's bank to the Korean entity's capital-escrow KRW or foreign-currency account with a strict purpose code matching the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act service schedule, typically classified as foreign direct investment contribution or share subscription. The receiving Tier-1 bank will pre-screen the remitter and beneficiary, confirm the entity charter, and within the statutory filing window submit the FDI report to KFEIS. The Korean LLC must be fully identified and, if paid-in capital exceeds the notification threshold, the foreign investor file a FIPA notice with the Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency or a designated foreign exchange bank. The funds thereafter cannot be commingled with operational revenue and must be designated as paid-in capital in the accounting records and registered before any dividend distribution or capital reduction.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For outbound day-to-day service payments such as subscription royalties, licensing, cloud infrastructure, and international consultants, the primary clearing rail is SWIFT MT103 through a domestic foreign exchange bank, supported by the underlying contract, commercial invoice, calculation evidence, and purpose code for software-or-services royalties. For large equipment bundled services related to PropTech hardware installation, commercial documentary collections or a revolving documentary LC may be issued, although LC is not the standard rail for pure SaaS settlements. Operational KRW payments within South Korea are cleared via BIZWIRE or Fedwire-equivalent domestic bulk transfer using the bank's API; foreign suppliers must be paid only after KYC of the payee and post-transaction AML review. All outbound foreign remittances above the threshold require completion of the KFEIS reporting form and, where applicable, withholding tax proof for Korean-sourced income.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable KRW/USD forward contracts with a certified foreign exchange bank, limited to transparent underlying commercial exposure and generally capped at 110% of forecast export/import flows to satisfy the Real Demand Principle
FX option structures purchased from a licensed Korean bank to hedge subscription revenue and dividend remittance timing, including vanilla calls and puts with deliverable KRW settlement

Cross-currency basis swaps or interest-rate swaps matching USD-denominated venture debt or shareholder loans against KRW operating cash flow, provided the notional is tied to the entity's actual borrowings

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not ordinarily permissible for Korean resident entities because the KRW is deliverable onshore and the regulators restrict offshore NDF use; an NDF may only be available through a special non-resident branch structure or with MOEF approval when used against an recognised offshore investment exposure

stage_4.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Exports of digital SaaS services receive export proceeds through a domestic foreign exchange bank within 18 months of the invoice date; the bank counts 100% of the proceeds as repatriated if deposited into a domestic foreign-currency account or converted to KRW at the prevailing market rate. No fractional surrender ratio exists, and optional conversion is at the entity's election.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low viability. Offshore digital EMIs such as Wise or Revolut Business are not licensed to maintain KRW deposit accounts or to serve as the primary clearing or settlement rail for a Korean resident corporate entity under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Electronic Financial Transactions Act. These EMIs may be used only as a billing front end for non-KRW collection but must be linked to a licensed Korean Tier-1 bank for the actual KRW settlement and compliance reporting.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Yes. Korean banks require statutory directors or their authorized representatives with notarized and apostilled power of attorney to appear in-branch for KYC verification. Remote video KYC is generally not sufficient for opening a corporate account, although pre-interview remote screens are accepted. A non-resident director may be permitted through a consular-proved power of attorney only if the bank's compliance committee approves, but at least one responsible person must attend in person.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholding chain exceeding one intermediate holding layer, triggering enhanced due diligence under FATF Recommendation 24.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A complete corporate registry chain, certified UBO declaration for every natural person holding 25% or more, trust or SPV organizational documents, audited financials of intermediate SPVs, tax certificates of all shareholders, and a notarized statement of source of wealth for the ultimate investors.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PropTech SaaS platform receiving funds from real estate brokerage or rental escrow flows may be mischaracterised as an unlicensed money service business.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed SaaS contract, detailed functional description proving software-only provision, third-party AML review of the platform, customer due-diligence samples, tenant screening and payment records, valuation methodology of the platform's fee, and an external audit report showing no comingled client funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The Korean resident director is a nominee rather than the ultimate controller, creating a red flag for shell corporate use.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A Director's Declaration of Nonexecutive Status where not applicable, employment contract, tax filing history of the director in Korea, office lease in the company name, payroll and national pension payment records for local staff, and board minutes appointing the director as bank relationship signatory.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial capital injection from offshore jurisdictions with ambiguous source-of-funds documentation, particularly where founding equity was earned through cryptocurrency or digital assets.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A 12-month bank statement of the remitting investor, source-of-wealth explanation with employment or incorporations contracts, exchange and brokerage statements if digital assets are involved, the signed investment agreement, valuation cap table, and a certified statement that the funds are free of sanctions exposure.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injection should be routed as an SWIFT MT103 from the foreign investor's bank to the Korean Tier-1 bank with purpose code for direct investment under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act; prior to wiring, the investor must file a foreign-investment report with a designated foreign exchange bank or the Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency. The receiving bank will open a foreign-investment registration account, verify the entity documentation, collect the capital verification certificate after attorney or CPA confirmation, and supply the company with the Approval of Foreign Investment notice. All KRW conversions must be executed onshore at the prevailing spot rate and reported to KFEIS.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For service and SaaS export disbursements, use SWIFT MT103 with the appropriate Korean standard currency code for software/IT services and maintain a database of invoices and proof-of-performance. For physical equipment or real-estate-related ancillary hardware purchases, commercial letters of credit and documentary collections may be used, but the primary cross-border trade settlement for PropTech SaaS is direct MT103 to vendors, service providers, and dividend beneficiaries. International card clearing networks (Visa/Mastercard) local acquiring settlements can be used for small ticket revenue, to be swept daily into the KRW operating account through the acquiring bank's clearing file.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable FX forwards with Korean Tier-1 banks on a Hedging Underlying Trade basis, with no net speculative positions
FX options, including euro dollar style European options, covering SaaS subscription receivables
Cross-currency interest rate swaps only for existing KRW debt or operational liquidity swaps with a licensed bank
NDFs are not permitted for Korean resident entities under ordinary onshore rules; only non-resident counterparties may be permitted to use NDFs against KRW with special KFEIS approval

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return and Local Income Tax Surtax Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) and competent local government (si/gun/gu)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a December 31 fiscal year-end, file by March 31 of the following year; a one-month extension to April 30 is available when financial statements are audited by an independent certified public accountant.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing triggers an additional penalty of 20% of the underpaid corporate tax (10% where no tax is payable); underreporting penalty of 20%; late-payment interest accrues at 0.022% per day (approximately 8.03% per annum). Persistent delinquency may cause collection procedures, asset seizure, designation as a high-risk delinquent taxpayer, and after prolonged non-payment administrative strike-off of the business registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-Added Tax Return (Semi-Annual and Monthly Large-Taxpayer Filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) via HomeTax system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For the January-June VAT period, file by July 25 of the same year; for the July-December VAT period, file by January 25 of the following year. A taxpayer with prior-year taxable turnover above KRW 20 billion must instead file monthly by the 25th of the following month.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file triggers a 10% additional tax on the unpaid VAT; underdeclaration or excessive deduction penalties also apply at 10%; late-payment interest accrues daily at 0.022%; repeated non-compliance may result in criminal penalties for fraudulent evasion and business registration strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Withholding Tax and Payroll Compliance Remittance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) for tax withheld from wages, bonuses, dividends, interest and foreign payments
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Monthly withheld taxes must be remitted by the 10th day of the following month; the annual labor income tax integrated settlement report is due by March 10 of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to withhold properly carries a 10% withholding negligence tax; failure to pay withheld amounts further triggers a 20% additional tax plus daily late-payment interest of 0.022%; serious or intentional non-remittance can result in criminal fines and forfeiture of tax benefits.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign-Invested Company Annual Report (Foreign Investment Status Report)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: KOTRA (Invest KOREA) / Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The annual foreign investment status report must be submitted during the January 1 to June 30 window following the relevant calendar year; any material change in foreign equity ownership or registered investment items must be reported within 30 days of the change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or falsely filing the report may attract an administrative fine of up to KRW 3 million (approximately USD 2,250); the foreign investor may lose statutory protection, exchange-rate guarantees, tax treaty benefits or tax exemption/abatement benefits and may be subject to correction orders.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory External Audit Report and Filing with Financial Supervisory Service
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) / DART electronic disclosure system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a December 31 year-end, the certified independent audit must be completed within six months after fiscal year-end (no later than June 30) and presented to the members; under the External Audit Act, the signed audit report must be filed with the FSS/DART by April 17 (or the next business day if the date falls on a weekend/holiday) unless an extended deadline is approved.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to appoint a statutory auditor without just cause may result in a civil fine of up to KRW 30 million (approximately USD 22,500); submission of false or misleading audit reports triggers criminal penalties and director disqualification; continued non-compliance can lead to regulatory sanctions, forced correction orders, and administrative strike-off action.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, a Yuhan Hoesa (LLC) is compulsorily subject to independent certified public accountant (CPA) audit if total assets at the immediately preceding fiscal year-end equal or exceed KRW 10 billion (approximately USD 7.6 million). Additional mandatory audit triggers apply if the entity is a listed or financial investment company, a public company under the Financial Investment Services and Capital Markets Act, or if it otherwise meets the delegated regulatory size criteria based on balance sheet assets, annual turnover and headcount. For a private PropTech SaaS LLC, the asset-based KRW 10 billion threshold is the primary statutory audit trigger.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) apply to all entities subject to statutory external audit; non-audited private Yuhan Hoesa entities may prepare financial statements under Korean GAAP (K-GAAP) issued by the Korean Accounting Standards Board, or may voluntarily apply K-IFRS. Full financial statements must be denominated in Korean won unless approved otherwise by the Financial Supervisory Service.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: A Yuhan Hoesa (LLC) is not required to file an annual UBO return to a central Korean registry. However, if the company is a foreign-invested enterprise, it must confirm its foreign investor composition annually between January 1 and June 30 through KOTRA/MOTIE. Under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, any material change in foreign ownership, including shareholding transfers that alter foreign investment status, must be reported within 30 days of the change. Internally, the company must maintain an accurate and current file of beneficial ownership information for Korean AML/CDD obligations, and all member transfers must be recorded in the member register and, where applicable, reported to the competent registry within the statutory 30-day registration window.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (list of members / Sajin myeongbu) or Register of Shareholders if structured as a stock company
Register of Directors (where directors are appointed)
Register of Charges, Pledges and Mortgages over shares or movable assets
Minute Book (minutes of member meetings and director meetings)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 800 - USD 1,500 per year (approximately KRW 1,050,000 - KRW 1,950,000) for registered office address and local corporate secretarial agent services in Seoul or other metropolitan cities.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,000 - USD 15,000 per year (approximately KRW 7,800,000 - KRW 19,500,000) for a certified independent audit, depending on revenue, transaction volume, complexity and auditor size.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% national corporate income tax on the highest marginal tranche (above KRW 300 billion), plus a 10% local income tax surcharge producing an effective top marginal rate of 26.4%
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Venture enterprise 50% corporate income tax reduction for five qualifying years; R&D expenditure tax credits for qualifying PropTech software development; free-zone foreign-investor corporate tax holiday; no patent-box regime; temporary tax credits for data-center and cloud infrastructure investments under the Restriction of Special Taxation Act

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Tax Base and Tax Amount Standard Return (Form 1101) and attached schedules, filed electronically through the National Tax Service HomeTax portal (hometax.go.kr)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, with half-yearly primary prepayment filings during the fiscal year and a single annual settlement return
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 3 months after the fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year Yuhan Hoesa the filing deadline is 31 March; a one-month extension can be requested with just cause, but tax due must be provisionally paid by the original deadline

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 – Corporation Identification and Residence Status
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the Korean business registration number, head office address, representative director, fiscal year, and whether the corporation is a domestic corporation or a foreign corporation under the Corporate Tax Act.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Yuhan Hoesa incorporated in Korea with a head office or effective place of management in Korea is a domestic corporation taxed on worldwide income. Non-resident shareholders must be listed in the foreign shareholder ledger with their country of tax residence. Incorrect residence classification creates Korean-source income misdeclaration exposure.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report total worldwide operating revenue from PropTech SaaS subscriptions, property-rental screening fees, data analytics, and cloud platform fees, net of returns and allowances, excluding value-added tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Revenue from non-Korean customers remains taxable in Korea because the Korean LLC is a resident taxpayer. Carefully characterize subscription fees versus licensing of digital software, because Korea treats royalty and service income differently for cross-border withholding purposes. Maintain a contemporaneous revenue recognition policy and delivery-location evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add back or exclude statutory non-taxable income, tax-exempt dividends received, certain public-purpose subsidies, and foreign-source income eligible for exemption only where expressly authorized.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not treat offshore cash held in Stripe or foreign bank accounts as exempt income. Foreign subsidiary dividend-received deductions and foreign-source income exclusions require a complete ownership chain and foreign tax credit schedule. Any attempt to classify SaaS income as non-taxable merely because the customer is abroad is a fatal error.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 – Statutory Adjustments and Non-Deductible Expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconcile K-IFRS or K-GAAP net income to accounting taxable income by adding back non-deductible expenses and deducting statutory reserves and deferral items.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Intercompany payments to non-resident shareholders are deductible only at arm’s length. The National Tax Service may disallow cross-border cost-sharing fees, management charges without substance, and related-party royalties lacking beneficial ownership. Interest deductions must also satisfy the Korea thin-capitalization 3:1 debt-to-equity restriction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 – Prior-Year Loss Carryforward and Taxable Income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Compute final taxable income after offsetting prior-year net operating losses, applying tax concessions, and aggregating all temporary and permanent differences.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses generally carry forward 10 years, with 15 years available for qualifying small and medium enterprises in designated loss years. If the Yuhan Hoesa was acquired merely to leverage an aged loss shell, the National Tax Service may deny the carryforward under the substance-over-form doctrine.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 – Progressive Corporate Income Tax Computation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply the national progressive corporate tax rates to taxable income: 9% on the first KRW 200 million, 19% on taxable income from KRW 200 million to KRW 20 billion, 21% on taxable income from KRW 20 billion to KRW 300 billion, and 24% above KRW 300 billion.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Because the Korean LLC is a domestic corporation, no non-resident corporate tax rate applies to the Korean entity itself. Non-resident shareholders are subject separately to dividend withholding tax on distributions. Use the rate schedule in force for the taxable year and ensure the computed national corporate income tax reconciles to Box 8.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Compute the local income tax surcharge equal to 10% of the national corporate income tax calculated in Box 6.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The local surcharge is not a deductible expense. A calendar-year filer must submit the simultaneous local income tax return with the national return; failure to file the surcharge is an automatic non-filing event. The effective top combined rate is 26.4%.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8 – Tax Credits, Foreign Tax Credit, Provisional Payments, and Net Tax Payable
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter investment tax credits, R&D employment credits, foreign tax credits, quarterly provisional tax payments, withholding credits, and prior installments, and compute the final balance due or refund.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The foreign tax credit is capped at the Korean corporate tax attributable to foreign-source income. Attach foreign tax vouchers and overseas tax returns. If the Korean company pays outbound dividends, interest, or royalties to non-residents, it must withhold statutory WHT and attach the DTA relief annex before reducing the rate; missing WHT disclosure is a fatal Box 8 compliance gap.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 9 – Transfer Pricing and International Transaction Disclosure
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declare all cross-border related-party transactions with non-resident shareholders, foreign affiliates, and offshore SaaS platform companies, including transaction amounts, counterparty, transfer-pricing method, and Local File or Master File availability.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Mandatory integrated TP disclosure arises when the revenue and related-party transaction thresholds are met. Select an approved arm’s length method and document the functional analysis, risks, and assets of the Korean entity. If the aggregate cross-border related-party transaction exceeds KRW 50 billion, the detailed TP schedules and contemporaneous documentation must be complete before filing. Failure to file triggers separate penalty exposure.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a 20% additional tax on the unpaid amount (40% for fraudulent or unlawful omission); underreporting triggers a 10% additional tax (20% if unlawful); late payment surcharge accrues at 0.022% per day from the due date; late or insufficient transfer-pricing documentation attracts separate penalty tax. Fraudulent evasion is prosecuted under the Punishment Act for Tax Evaders with criminal imprisonment and fines up to five times the evaded tax.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% (20% dividends withholding tax plus 2% local income tax surcharge; reduced further only if the tax treaty and beneficial-ownership conditions are satisfied)
